chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man is in need, so charity is sent to him, but he does not accept it as charity; he is held back by modesty, embarrassment, and withdrawal. Should we give it to him in a manner other than that, even though it is charity from us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. If it is zakat, he has the right to accept it. But if he does not accept it as zakat, do not give it to him. And it is not befitting for him to be embarrassed by what Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has imposed; it is merely an obligation of Allah for him, so he should not be embarrassed by it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a needy person refuses to accept zakat due to modesty?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the tension between preserving the recipient's dignity and fulfilling the divine obligation of zakat by distinguishing between the legal category of 'zakat' and the social act of 'gift-giving'. He instructs that if the recipient refuses the specific label of zakat due to modesty, the giver should withhold it rather than disguising it as a gift, emphasizing that zakat is a right prescribed by Allah, not a charity to be accepted with shame. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the sanctity of the obligation outweighs temporary social embarrassment, encouraging recipients to claim their due without hesitation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘The man happens to be needy, so I sent the charity (Zakāt) to him, but he did not accept it upon its aspect that it is the charity (Zakāt). Taking it from that makes him an introvert, and embarrassed, and withdrawn. Should I give it to him upon other than that aspect, and it is a charity (Zakāt) from us?’ So heasws said: ‘No. When it was Zakāt, so it is for him that he accepts it. But if he does not accept it upon its aspect as the Zakāt, so do not give it to him; and it is not befitting for him that he should be too embarrassed from what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Imposed. But rather, it is an Imposition of Allahazwj for him, therefore he should not be embarrassed from it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is needy and I send him charity (Zakat) but he does not accept as charity (Zakat); it causes him to be protective, shy and depressed. Can I give without the aspect of charity (Zakat) when it is charity (Zakat) from us?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is Zakat he must accept it and if he does not accept it with the aspect of Zakat, then do not give it to him. It is not proper for him to be shy about what Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made obligatory. It is only obligatory from Allah for him and he must not feel shy about it.’”
